meta.titulo: Ánfora · Work demo (fictional product) · Ramiro Bales
meta.descripcion: Ramiro Bales' test page: the landing page of a fictional product with real 3D, photoscanned materials and scroll-driven choreography, built with AI-assisted development and verified by hand.
s1.titulo: The jug that measures with shadow.
s1.sub: A fictional product built to show how I work.
s1.texto: Ánfora is a porcelain jug resting on a travertine base. No screen, no battery: a dial engraved in the stone shows how much water is left by the shadow the body casts. Scroll down to see the materials, the mechanism and how this page was made.
s1.pista: Scroll: the light moves, not the jug.
s2.titulo: Real porcelain, real stone, real clay.
s2.texto: Nothing procedural: the three materials are photoscanned surfaces published under CC0 by ambientCG, lit with a studio photographed by Poly Haven. What you see is each one's colour, relief and roughness map, measured on the original material.
s2.m1.uso: Body, handle and spout. Mean roughness of the map: 0.07. Glaze gloss with a 0.25 sheen for the translucent white.
s2.m2.uso: Base and dial. Mean roughness of the map: 0.03, a mirror polish. In the scene I raised it to 0.27: stone has to read as stone, not as glass.
s2.m3.uso: Lid with 48 ridges. Mean roughness of the map: 0.58, with the scan's occlusion and relief; the ridges are geometry, not texture.
s3.titulo: The shadow falls on the dial. That's all.
s3.texto: Full, the jug weighs more and sinks slightly into the seat of the base; empty, it rises. The body changes height and its shadow on the dial changes length: one mark per quarter litre. No sensors, no screen: a light, a stone and a reading.
s3.pista: Keep scrolling: the lid opens, the level drops and the number follows.
s4.d1.texto: Elliptical section, not round: the hand grips it edge-on and a full jug doesn't twist.
s4.d2.texto: A three-millimetre lip with the sharp edge inside: it cuts the stream and doesn't drip outside.
s4.d3.texto: Twenty-five millimetres of travertine with a four-millimetre chamfer: the weight stays low and the edge doesn't chip.
s4.d4.texto: Clay with forty-eight ridges: it grips with wet fingers and makes no sound when set down.
s5.brief.p: A porcelain jug with a travertine base that shows how much water is left by the shadow it casts. One camera and five stops tied to the scroll. CC0 photoscanned materials lit by a real environment. If there is no WebGL, or the person asked for less motion, an image of the same scene. Total weight under four megabytes and sixty frames per second on an integrated GPU.
s5.prompts.t: What I asked the agent for
s5.prompts.p: Geometry by revolution, with an elliptical-section handle, a spout that tapers and the lid's ridges as vertex displacement, not as texture. The dial as a decal on the stone. That what moves is the light and the camera, never the object on a loop, and that every drift dies out on its own after twelve seconds without events. That all text enters line by line tied to the scroll, except the first screen, which enters on load.
s5.iter.p: Every round ended in a full-resolution screenshot that I looked at before moving on. Below, the first pass of the scene and the final version: what changed between them are decisions, not luck.
s5.iter.antes.alt: First pass of the scene: the jug before the light and materials were adjusted
s5.iter.despues.alt: Final version of the scene with afternoon light and corrected materials
s5.cambiaria.p: A compressed model instead of geometry generated on load, a prefiltered environment cube instead of the HDR file, and a camera that follows the pointer's gesture with more character. What I wouldn't change: the screenshot overrules the opinion.
s5.cierre: This is a test page. The product doesn't exist; the method does.
pie.ficticio: Ánfora is a fictional product, made as a test page by Ramiro Bales. It doesn't exist, isn't sold and isn't manufactured.
